source.title: Learning curves theory for hierarchically compositional data with power-law distributed features
source.authors: Francesco Cagnetta; Hyunmo Kang; M. Wyart

record.tranche_reason: The study derives and empirically examines learning curves using synthetic hierarchical data and CNNs/transformers, rather than reproducing the original language-model scaling experiments.
record.gate_note: The study's own theoretical derivations and synthetic-model experiments bear on learning-curve shape and its dependence on the data-generation setup. Results cited from Kaplan et al., Hoffmann et al. and other work are not recorded as findings. Figure values are not tabulated numerically, so those rows use 'figure only'.
record.test_reason: The study derives and measures learning curves (test loss vs. training-set size P) for CNNs and transformers trained on synthetic hierarchical (RHM) data. These results bear on whether loss follows a power law in data (V1) and on how the exponent and curve shape depend on data structure (V7). The setting is new (synthetic grammar data, small models, data-limited regime), so this is T3 rather than a reproduction of the original method.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Add that the authors present the hierarchical structure of language as a prime candidate for explaining LLM scaling laws, since in next-token prediction the exponent comes from progressively resolving longer-range correlations rather than from the Zipf feature distribution.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes synthetic probabilistic context-free grammars and trains CNNs and transformers; it does not reproduce the original parameter/token/compute sweeps on language-model pretraining.
record.method_sensitivity: The learning-curve form depends on task (classification versus next-token prediction), the distribution and layer of production rules, and hierarchy-related settings such as m, v and L. For next-token prediction the Zipf exponent affects local details and residual loss but not the stated asymptotic exponent.
record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning, Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 267 (2025)
record.problems: The evidence concerns simplified synthetic hierarchical data rather than natural text or large language models. Several results are presented only in figures, without numerical curve values or plotted uncertainty bars. The study itself notes that real-data tree topology may vary and context-dependent effects may not be captured by its model.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant result conditions were left out. Figures 3 and 8 show rescaled versions of the same curves already recorded in R13 and R25; those are represented as aggregate curve-collapse rows rather than duplicating each underlying curve.

untested.parts: Scaling in parameters and compute; natural-text pretraining; real language models. Only training-set size P is varied, on synthetic RHM data with small transformers.
Entire version: no fits on small runs extrapolated to larger runs.
Entire version: no shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
Entire version: no other modalities, repeated-data, fine-tuning or transfer regimes.

Fitting methods, parameter-counting conventions, training schedules, compute-optimal split, and comparison with published exponents. The hierarchy parameters (m, v, s) are not varied empirically in the deep-transformer next-token experiments.

missing.what: Exact s^ℓ-gram cross-entropies L_ℓ vs. ℓ for varying a, averaged over 32 RHM realisations. They show L_ℓ − L∞(a) is independent of a and follows the uniform scaling. This is computed, not trained, and supports the V7 limits_scope verdict.

Setup checks: CNN width beyond H=512, transformer heads nh up to 64, and embedding width up to 4×nh×v do not change the results. This confirms a data-limited regime in which model size is not the bottleneck (relevant to V1's other-factors condition).

record.verdict_notes: All empirical evidence is figure-only: no numeric exponents or error bars are given, and agreement with theory is asserted in the text. Classification rows (CNNs, root label) are not language-model loss; they bear on V7 only through the general claim that exponent and curve shape depend on data structure. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: Parameter-count and compute scaling; ordinary language-model pretraining and real text data. The empirical tests use synthetic RHM data and vary training-set size P.
The study does not fit laws on small runs and test predictions on runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep over model size and token count.
No controlled comparison of depth, width or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No tests of other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning or transfer. Synthetic hierarchical sequences are not a test of those regimes.

The study varies task and synthetic data-generation properties, but does not compare fitting methods, parameter-count conventions, training schedules, or published exponent estimates; it does not study compute-optimal allocation.

rows.subject: RHM theoretical analysis (root classification)
rows.operation_detail: Derived the asymptotic classification error for Zipf-distributed production rules.
rows.measure: classification error versus training-set size P
rows.value: ε(P) ∼ P^(-a/(1+a)); pre-asymptotic scale controlled by the hierarchy
rows.note: The paper says the Zipf exponent determines the asymptotic decay while the hierarchy controls the size of the pre-asymptotic phase.
rows.check: Theoretical derivation (Eq. 8), not an empirical measurement. The task is root classification by CNNs, not language-model loss, so it bears on V7 only by analogy (exponent set by the data distribution).

rows.subject: RHM theoretical analysis (next-token prediction)
rows.operation_detail: Derived the next-token learning-curve scaling from reconstruction of hierarchical structure.

conditions.value: RHM with Zipf-distributed level-1 production rules

rows.measure: average cross-entropy loss
rows.value: L(P) ∼ P^(-log(m/v^(s-1))/(2 log m)); P-independent factors neglected
rows.note: The stated exponent depends on the hierarchical structure, not on the Zipf exponent a.
rows.check: Eq. 12 for the uniform RHM is cited from Cagnetta & Wyart (2024). The study's own contribution is the argument (Eqs. 13–18) that Zipf level-1 rules leave this exponent unchanged. The row is theory, not a measurement, and should be marked as partly a cited result.

source_check.problem: Provenance needs preserving: Eq. 12 is attributed to Cagnetta & Wyart (2024); this study argues that nonuniform level-1 rules retain its exponent.
